correctness.rationale: Independently replayed the complete 177147-state domain using memoized paths and first-repeat dictionaries, not either frozen implementation. Each successor uses the displayed adjacency and the old configuration, with unconditional GHM 1->2->0 and contact-only CCA advances. On first repetition within a path the suffix beginning at the previous occurrence has the least period and zero entry depth; a reverse pass assigns the prefix, or assigns the entire path from a previously classified tail. Every input is covered. There are zero pointwise period mismatches and the common populations at periods 1,3,4 are 17397,23346,136404. Recurrent-state totals are CCA (3,3060,4752) and GHM (1,3060,1200); the replay checked recurrent containment, identical period-three sets and matching successors on every GHM recurrent state. The orbit counts follow by division by least period. Every one of the 21 CCA and 27 GHM depth-period histogram cells matches both frozen tables. The only deepest cells are CCA (8,3) with 108 starts and GHM (10,3) with 36. The displayed graph was also checked independently to be simple, 3-connected planar, non-Hamiltonian and of size (11,18), identifying it as Herschel by the uniqueness for those parameters.
residual_risks: The exact label-to-edge transcription in the University of Washington drawing was not verified visually; its extracted text only exposes the title. The displayed graph was identified up to isomorphism independently, which suffices for these labelled-state census counts and pointwise assertions under common relabelling.
The scope is the stated rules and graph, not arbitrary thresholds, schedules or a graph family. Equal period basins are not equal individual orbit basins.

evidence: Gravner–Lyu–Sivakoff gives a maximum-walk description and synchronization criterion, Doba gives GHM asymptotics and cycle-density results, and 6edafe27dc02 gives exact same-start excitation recovery and p_H dividing p_C.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These results govern synchronization, clock recovery or rates; the inspected statements do not enumerate Herschel periods or transients. GHM updates already obey the CCA contact conditions from time two: a color-one vertex has a former exciter now in state two, and a color-two vertex has one from two steps earlier now in state zero. Thus inclusion and shared transitions on the GHM recurrent set follow generally and are not counted as distinct Herschel contributions.

evidence: Petersen has 4800 matched starts with (p_C,p_H)=(8,4); Heawood has period-halving mismatch channels. For a genuine CCA period-three orbit on a connected graph, each vertex advances either all three times or not at all; a rotating neighbor would force a stationary vertex to advance, so connectivity makes every vertex advance, which also obeys GHM.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Divisibility plus common synchronization and the newly verified support {1,3,4} would entail pointwise equality on Herschel. They do not yield the support itself or its basin sizes, depth histograms, or period-four recurrent counts. The general period-three orbit argument likewise does not give the count of 3060 states.

value.rationale: Herschel is a natural extremal irregular polyhedral graph for comparing two closely related excitable automata. The exact equality of period selection, alongside four-cycle population disparity and different maximal clocks, separates identical eventual periodicity from equality of the recurrent sets and transients. The census is a useful exact benchmark beside biclique agreement and period halving on other sparse graphs, not a claim that non-Hamiltonicity enforces equality.
residual_risks: Graph-specific finite result; no causal explanation or extension to polyhedral graphs is established.
